deep.headline: Numbers, runway, and the way the money actually works.
deep.lede: Pricing, channel approach and the revenue model; then distribution in detail; then where AGF lands against the field.

items.title: Price is not the negotiation
items.body: Once a sales team has a customer, price is not the negotiation. The Relay at $199. The Relay at $249. The Relay at $299. Sales went up each time. Burmester at €5,999 packaging a $200-class device for convenience. The lesson is uncomfortable but true: **premium buyers do not want a discount. They want a reason.**

items.title: Price the package, not the unit
items.body: Price the package, not the unit. Convenience, integration, and context are the luxury product. The unit is a participant.

items.title: Curated third-party fills the floor
items.body: Lower price categories filled with curated third-party partner product. Presented honestly, humbly, recognizing product gaps. This approach must be backed by numbers — but the net positive is real: increased revenue, increased brand loyalty, educational feedback into our own product teams. **A Bose-like approach.**

sections.title: Hardware-led with a codec and OS halo
sections.body: **Hardware-led with codec/OS halo.** Direct hardware margin from Green Room sales (premium, appointment-driven). l'Art codec licensing is *not* the river — third parties adopt **stereOS** (application-specific implementation), not the codec itself. Performance content revenue is **50/50 split** with artists in perpetuity on broadcast-mixed l'Art versions; standard stereo is artist-owned. Owners receive permanent virtual all-access pass to live content.

sections.title: Three phases over five years
sections.body:
**Phase 1 (Year 1):** Inaugural product line ships from existing IP base. Single flagship venue (PoC). Channel introductions to stranded independents.

**Phase 2 (Years 2–3):** Second-wave AGF community franchises — venues replicating the FoH/Balcony/Green Room blueprint globally. l'Art codec adoption seeded through Balcony installations.

**Phase 3 (Years 3–5):** stereOS third-party adoption. Acquisition / hostile-service / integration decision for ten-ton gorillas. AGF as future bank-roller for stranded distribution channels.

sections.title: Distribution — the future bank-roller.
sections.body: Channel partners are owner-operators, often 20+ years in. They built the reputations of Polk, Definitive Tech, McIntosh, et al. Now they are treated like disposable assets because they do not hit spreadsheet numbers — but they cannot be fired either, because the bank *needs* a global distribution spine. AGF positions itself as the **future bank-roller, critically better than the devil they know**: lower price categories filled with curated third-party partner product, our line moving upward, the flagship landing just above Focal's consumer offering (~$5K USD).

sections.title: Third-party fills the floor; AGF owns the ceiling
sections.body: **Curated third-party fills the price floor; AGF owns the price ceiling.** Lower categories backed by partner product (presented honestly, with brand-humility). AGF flagship lands just above Focal consumer (~$5K). The package — not the unit — is the negotiation. The Burmester €5,999 lesson applied across the whole channel.

sections.title: The map: price against prestige
sections.lede: Average flagship price on a log scale against prestige. AGF lands just above Focal's consumer flagship and well below the incumbents that define the ceiling.
sections.note: Prestige scores are the source document's own estimates, not a measured index. Prices are the average flagship price the document assigns each brand. The cards below carry the same data.

sections.title: Where AGF lands
sections.lede: Every direct competitor below either opens a seam (consolidated, struggling, or closed) or defines the ceiling AGF is happy to sit just below. The aspirational tier survived; the ownership consolidated. The opening is the gap between the struggling incumbent and the $250K outlier.

items.title: Bang & Olufsen
items.pull: Luxury electronics — the comparable spiritual archetype
list: FY2007/08 peak revenue **~$853M USD** (≈ $1.25B in 2026 dollars)
FY2023/24 revenue **$402M** — less than half the peak
Public, Copenhagen-listed, decades into a slow decline
items.body: **Spiritual successor** to the era when B&O stood alone. Same archetype: appointment-driven, design-led, premium-only. AGF inherits the customer-acquisition discipline and the *no shoulder-to-shoulder fight* posture — the original B&O playbook, executed with 2026 technology.
kv: Opening
B&O's struggle vacates the 'lone luxury electronics archetype' chair. AGF takes the seat, with a venue model B&O never built.

items.title: Krell
list: Closed **June 18, 2024** following the death of owner/CEO Rondi D'Agostino
Service resumed **March 2025**; son Kristofer awarded **70%+ ownership Feb 2025**
Reopening through 2025 — re-establishing distribution, dealer trust still soft
items.body: **The Instrument fills this vacuum.** With Krell offline through 2024–2025 and the rebuild taking time to re-earn dealer/reviewer trust, the high-current aspirational chair is open. Boutique semis + GaN mono-block + FPGA give AGF a credible halo claim during the gap.
kv: Opening
12–24 month window where the aspirational halo seat has no obvious occupant. The Instrument lands inside the window.

items.title: Focal
list: **Consumer flagship ~$5K USD** — the established price ceiling for serious consumer audio
Now under Barco / VerVent (April 2026 acquisition, $135M) — distribution stable
Sells **~1,000 pcs/month** of flagship reference with a focused rep firm
items.body: **AGF positions just above Focal's consumer flagship.** The Instrument sits at $5K+ as a deliberate ceiling-tap, leveraging the reference Focal already established without competing for it shoulder-to-shoulder.
kv: Opening
Focal validated that the consumer market can absorb $5K halo product at meaningful volume. AGF inherits the price discovery and adds the venue + content moat.

items.title: Burmester
list: **€5,999** packaging for what AGF identified at Munich High-End as a **$200-class device** with above-average performance
Burmester executive: "the performance is above average, but you seem to have figured out some details we haven't — we package it with clients for convenience at €5,999"
items.body: **Genuine value at premium pricing.** Burmester proves the pricing model works (premium buyers want a reason, not a discount). AGF takes the same packaging logic and applies it to genuinely better technology — the moat is the delta between what AGF delivers and what is repackaged.
kv: Opening
The market accepts €5,999 packaging on $200 hardware. AGF can charge premium prices for premium technology and still look like the value play.

items.title: Dan D'Agostino
list: **$250K monoblocks** moving into Dolby Atmos maximalists
Rebuilt under his own name after the Krell PE rug-pull — proves a founder can survive consolidation and reach the ceiling on the rebound
items.body: **Defines the ceiling.** AGF is not chasing $250K monoblocks. The fact that the ceiling exists at that height — and customers exist who pay it — proves the prestige-audio market still has room above Focal and below the outlier. AGF lives in that gap.
kv: Opening
Confirms a meaningful ceiling exists for prestige audio. AGF needs only to occupy the territory just above Focal, with the option to climb later.

items.title: AGF
items.pull: Where AGF lands — just above Focal, well below the ceiling
list: Inaugural lineup spans Over-Ear → Symphony → Instrument
Symphony lands at $2,990 retail with a $29,990 review-tier anchor
Venue + content moat that no incumbent has built
items.body: **The seam between Focal and the ceiling.** AGF inherits B&O's archetype, fills Krell's vacuum, leverages Burmester's pricing logic, and lives just above Focal — with a venue model none of them have.
kv: Opening
AGF is the position itself: spiritual successor to a vacated archetype, halo without the $250K ask, value at premium pricing.

sections.title: The seam
sections.body: B&O struggles. Krell reopens. Focal sets the consumer ceiling. Burmester proves the pricing model. D'Agostino proves the ceiling exists. **AGF lands just above Focal, with B&O's archetype, Krell's vacuum, Burmester's pricing logic, and a venue model none of them have.**
